For the same 70 tablets you pay about $4.87 with Equate and $38.97 with Claritin.
Against it: Inactive ingredients differ. What differs
We don't earn anything from these links. Details
Read the label. This compares labels and published evidence. It isn't medical advice. Inactive ingredients (fillers, dyes, flavours) can differ, which matters if you have allergies. Ask a pharmacist, doctor or vet if you're unsure.
Why the extra money buys little
Both are loratadine 10 mg once-daily tablets, and Equate is labelled 'Compare to Claritin 24 Hour active ingredient'.
What we checked
Walmart's Claritin listing shows loratadine 10 mg tablets, 70 count, for $38.97 (55.7 cents each). The Equate listing shows loratadine USP 10 mg tablets, 300 count (2 bottles of 150), for $20.88 (7.0 cents each).
Worth knowing: The Equate 300-count was marked out of stock online when checked, so the price may move. Kirkland AllerClear (loratadine 10 mg, 365 count) at Costco is another low-cost option.
Where the brand wins, and what differs
What Equate doesn't match, from the same records as the saving.
Inactive ingredients differ.

Questions
Is Equate the same as Claritin?
Equate has the same active ingredient as Claritin: loratadine 10 mg. Same active ingredient(s), same strength, same dosage form, confirmed from the official label. Both labels were confirmed from primary sources.
What is different about Equate?
Inactive ingredients differ.
How much cheaper is Equate than Claritin?
Equate costs 7.0¢ per tablet against 56¢ for Claritin, 88% less, at the US prices we checked in November 2026.
Where can I buy Equate?
We checked the price at Walmart in November 2026. Prices change, so check at the store before you buy.
